summary: Carlo Giussani was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863), under Giuseppe Bardelli, under Albrecht Weber (1863), and under Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1866).
Carlo Jamelle Harris is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA in philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at SOAS, Somerville College, Oxford, Keio University, and under Shigeru Gorai. She served as a lecturer at the University of Cambridge and president of The Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the National University of San Marcos. She held posts at the IIBS (1989), the Nyingma Institute (1996), and the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (~1989–2018).

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001. She has held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008), Ruhr University Bochum, and Käte Hamburger Kolleg.

Carol A. Breckenridge was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1976) and held a position at the University of Chicago (~1982–1993).

Carol S. Anderson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago and studied under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman. She served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Geshe Thubten Ngawang. She held posts at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, CIHTS, and the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).
Carola S. Carstens is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg in 2005 and held a post at Rice University (1998–1999).
Carole M. Cusack is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan is an anthropologist and Tibetologist who studied at Colgate and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler. She joined the University of Colorado as Assistant Professor of Anthropology (~2001–2009).

Caroline Humphrey is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, religious, and Indic studies who earned degrees from Cambridge and Leeds, studying under Edmund Leach. She taught at the University of Cambridge (1971–2010) and held fellowships at Girton and King's Colleges.

Caroline Rhys Davids was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at UCL under George Croom Robertson and with T. W. Rhys Davids. She held posts at the Pali Text Society, University of Manchester, and SOAS.

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts at Ohio State University and Denison University (attested 1990).
Carson Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997 and took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Chicago Divinity School under Joseph M. Kitagawa. She served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Elaine Prueitt is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Rochester and earned her PhD from Emory University in 2016 under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an Indologist and historian who earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1977–1984) and served there as an Assistant Professor from approximately 1980 to 2021.

Catherine Ludvik is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who received her PhD from the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse. She has held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.
Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Kent (~1983–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.
